questions.q: What is the real skill this lesson teaches, underneath the Thornbury example?
options: Requirements clarification — turning a vague ask into a specific, answerable requirement
Writing T-SQL joins
Choosing between Import and DirectQuery in Power BI
Formatting DAX measures for a non-technical reader
questions.explain: This lesson is entirely about turning "show me how we're doing" into a specific, written requirement before any SQL or Power BI is touched.

questions.q: In the clarified requirement, what grouping level was chosen for "product categories," and why?
options: Product category (the top level of Production.ProductCategory), because the pricing review is a category-level conversation
Product subcategory, because it gives more detail
Individual product, because that's the most granular option available
Sales territory, because that's how most AdventureWorks2012 reports are grouped
questions.explain: The follow-up conversation settled on the top-level category grouping specifically, because subcategory detail would be more than the pricing review meeting needs.

questions.q: Why does the clarified requirement ask for total sales amount AND order count, rather than just one metric?
options: So the manager can see whether a category's revenue is driven by more orders or by bigger ones
Because AdventureWorks2012 only stores those two columns
Because Power BI requires at least two measures on every report
Order count is required for every GROUP BY query regardless of the business question
questions.explain: Both metrics side by side let the manager distinguish a category that's up because of order volume from one that's up because of bigger average orders.

questions.q: Which of these is explicitly OUT of scope for this Beginner project?
options: Pricing recommendations — deciding what to do about pricing is the meeting's job, not the dashboard's
Showing total sales amount for the current quarter
Showing order count for the current quarter
Grouping the data by product category
questions.explain: The report shows how categories are performing; it deliberately stops short of recommending pricing changes, which is what the meeting itself is for.

questions.q: What makes a written requirement "specific enough," according to this lesson?
options: You could hand it to a teammate and they'd build the same report back
It is at least three paragraphs long
It lists every column in every AdventureWorks2012 table
It avoids mentioning the stakeholder by name
questions.explain: The lesson's test for a specific requirement is whether a teammate, given only that sentence, would build the same report you have in mind.
